question: In knowledge distillation, the teacher model is typically a larger (more powerful) network than the student model. Has there been work showing that the teacher model is size-matched or smaller (but perhaps more targeted in knowledge) than the student model, and for knowledge transfer to still be effective?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: States that in conventional knowledge distillation the teacher is a larger, more powerful (cumbersome) model — possibly an ensemble — and the goal is transferring its generalization ability to a small student.
examples: In standard KD the teacher is a cumbersome larger network and the student a small model trained to generalize in the same way as the teacher
Conventionally, distillation transfers knowledge from a large ensemble or powerful model into a smaller student model

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: Explains that knowledge is transferred by using the teacher's class probabilities (predictive distribution) as soft targets for training the student, possibly on a separate transfer set; ensemble soft targets may be arithmetic or geometric means of member distributions.
examples: The cumbersome model's predictive distribution is used as soft targets when training the small model
When the teacher is a large ensemble, an arithmetic or geometric mean of the members' predictive distributions forms the soft targets

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: Identifies work (Revisiting KD via Label Smoothing Regularization) showing that a weak student model can transfer its soft targets to the larger teacher and improve it — reverse knowledge distillation (Re-KD).
examples: Re-KD: letting student models teach teacher models via their soft targets showed the weak student can improve the teacher
Reverse KD: transferring soft targets from student to teacher yields significant enhancement of the teacher

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: Identifies the companion experiment (De-KD) showing that a poorly-trained teacher with worse performance than the student can still remarkably enhance the student model.
examples: De-KD: a teacher with worse accuracy than the student still boosts student performance
Poorly-trained teachers were shown to enhance student models remarkably, contradicting the common belief

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: Explicitly characterizes these results as contradictory/counterintuitive relative to the common belief that weak models cannot provide reliable similarity information between categories — motivating a rethinking of KD.
examples: The common belief is that weak models cannot provide reliable similarity information, but experiments show contradictory results
Both a weak student teaching the teacher and a weak teacher teaching the student are effective, counterintuitively

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: Explains the results by re-interpreting KD as a regularization term, connected to Label Smoothing Regularization, where smoothed labels replace one-hot labels during training.
examples: KD is reinterpreted as a form of regularization akin to label smoothing regularization
LSR regularizes training by replacing one-hot labels with smoothed ones, mirroring what soft targets do in KD

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: States that dark knowledge does not just contain similarity information between categories; a model lacking sufficient similarity information can still provide dark knowledge that enhances other models.
examples: Dark knowledge is argued to contain more than similarity information, so even models lacking reliable similarity can enhance others
Even without enough similarity information, a model can provide dark knowledge that enhances another model

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: Notes that high-entropy soft targets carry much more information per training case, and that a student trained to generalize the way a good teacher does performs better on test data than one trained normally.
examples: High-entropy soft targets provide much more information per training case
A small model trained to generalize like a well-generalizing ensemble does better on test data than one trained normally

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: Concludes affirmatively that size-matched or smaller/weaker teachers have been shown to enable effective knowledge transfer (via Re-KD/De-KD from 'Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization'), with effectiveness explained by regularization from dark knowledge rather than teacher capacity.
examples: Yes — follow-up work demonstrates effective knowledge transfer from weaker or size-matched models
The answer concludes teacher strength is not a prerequisite; KD acts as regularization through dark knowledge
